context.title: Living Water at Jacob's Well
context.summary: At a well in Samaria, Jesus offers a Samaritan woman living water, reveals her past, and tells her he is the Messiah. Her town believes. Back in Galilee he heals a royal official's son by a word.
context.background: Samaritans descended largely from northern Israelites who mixed with peoples Assyria settled in the land (2 Kings 17). They accepted only the five books of Moses and worshipped on Mount Gerizim, the 'mountain' in v. 20. Jews and Samaritans had a long, bitter hostility.

customs.term: The sixth hour at the well
customs.note: About noon, if counted from sunrise. Women usually drew water in the cooler morning or evening, so a lone woman at midday may hint at her isolation.
Everyday speech for fresh running water from a spring, as opposed to still water in a cistern. Jesus gives the phrase a deeper meaning.

watchFor: The woman's understanding grows: 'a Jew', 'Sir', 'a prophet', 'the Christ' (vv. 9–29).
The Samaritans call Jesus 'the Saviour of the world' (v. 42).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: John
people.summary: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30:23, 24), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.”

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Judea
places.summary: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Sychar
places.summary: Liar or drunkard (see Isa. 28:1, 7), has been from the time of the Crusaders usually identified with Sychem or Shechem (John 4:5).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Cana
places.summary: Reedy, a town of Galilee, near Capernaum. Here our Lord wrought his first miracle, the turning of water into wine (John 2:1-11; 4:46). It is also mentioned as the birth-place of Nathanael (21:2).

places.name: Capernaum
places.summary: Nahum’s town, a Galilean city frequently mentioned in the history of our Lord. It is not mentioned in the Old Testament. After our Lord’s expulsion from Nazareth (Matt. 4:13-16; Luke 4:16-31), Capernaum became his “own city.”
